Main result: the chapter's repeated rule 'AWS has no synchronous cross-Region replication' is refuted by the DynamoDB Developer Guide (MRSC global tables, GA June 30, 2025); it appears in five places (fast table, deep how-it-works, quiz q009, card c007, speak s02).

findings.section: A second Region protects against Region failure but replicates asynchronously (step 3, plain table, Exam trap aws-map-trap-sync-replication-across-regions)
findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** AWS offers no "synchronous replica in another Region". <!-- trap: aws-map-trap-sync-replication-across-regions -->
findings.evidence: The linked fact global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication quotes a whitepaper sentence that ends 'at this time' (docs/whitepapers .../regional-services: 'AWS does not provide a synchronous Cross-Region replication feature at this time.'). A newer AWS page contradicts it. full:amazondynamodb-developerguide (Global tables read consistency): 'With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns, and strongly consistent read operations on any replica always return the latest version of an item.' Same guide (Choosing a consistency mode): 'MRSC global tables support a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero.' docs/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DocumentHistory row dated June 30, 2025: 'DynamoDB now supports Multi-Region Strong Consistency (MRSC) for global tables with optional witness Region. MRSC allows strongly consistent reads across Regions with a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero during regional failures.' GA June 30, 2025 is more than 3 months before any exam date, so it is examinable (RULINGS rule 7). Step 3 ('The copy runs behind.'), the plain table row 'Survive a Region failure | A second Region | Asynchronous' and the trap all teach a false absolute. Fix: amend the fact (currency vote: stale), teach 'most cross-Region replication is asynchronous (S3 CRR, cross-Region read replicas, DynamoDB global tables in the default MREC mode); DynamoDB global tables with MRSC replicate synchronously, with RPO zero, in exactly three Regions', and add a Changed recently note (old: no synchronous cross-Region feature; new: DynamoDB MRSC, 2025-06-30; older exam questions may assume asynchronous only).
findings.resolution: fix-02: absolute removed. Step 3 now reads 'An asynchronous copy runs behind' with the verified fact global-infrastructure-async-cross-region-replication-may-lose-data plus 'Services differ.'; table cell 'Often asynchronous'; trap aws-map-trap-sync-replication-across-regions rewritten as a stem pattern (an option promising no loss after failover to an asynchronous copy); Say it scoped. Fact global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication rejected with facts amend --reject (no dependents left). Not done: the DynamoDB MRSC exception and a Changed recently entry, because the canon has no verified MRSC fact (no dynamodb facts yet); the DynamoDB chapter (28) must register and teach it. The H3 heading '... but replicates asynchronously' is a brief section id (L905), so the orchestrator should change it in brief.json (suggested: '... and most copies run behind').

findings.section: Choose it or not (table row 'Synchronous copies?')
findings.quote: | Synchronous copies? | No | Yes: [replicate data synchronously between Availability Zones](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-az-latency-single-digit-ms) | No: AWS has no [synchronous Cross-Region replication feature](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication) |
findings.evidence: Same refutation as claims-001: full:amazondynamodb-developerguide 'With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns' and DocumentHistory (June 30, 2025) 'MRSC allows strongly consistent reads across Regions with a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero during regional failures.' The 'A second Region' cell states 'No' as an absolute. Fix with the same wording as claims-001 (for example 'Usually no: most cross-Region copies are asynchronous; DynamoDB MRSC global tables are the exception'), linked to a new verified fact.
findings.resolution: fix-02: row is now 'Synchronous copies possible? | No second zone | Yes: you can replicate data synchronously between Availability Zones | Often not: an asynchronously replicated datastore can lose writes', linked to verified facts. No absolute left.

findings.section: Question 7 (aws-map-q009): Why not option 2, and Twin
findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "a Region failure must lose no committed write" instead: no AWS replication feature meets it, because AWS [does not provide a synchronous Cross-Region replication feature](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication).
findings.evidence: The Twin is false: full:amazondynamodb-developerguide (Choosing a consistency mode) 'MRSC global tables support a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero.' and (Evacuating an offline Region) 'MRSC tables support a recovery point objective (RPO) of zero.' A Region failure that must lose no committed write is exactly what DynamoDB MRSC global tables are for. The Why-not of option 2 ('so this replica cannot be built with an AWS feature') rests on the same stale fact; the key (options 1 and 3) can stay because the stem says 'managed relational database' and DynamoDB is NoSQL, but the reason must be the relational engine's replication (cross-Region read replicas / Aurora Global Database are asynchronous), not 'AWS has no synchronous feature'. Also check Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters (relational, multi-Region strong consistency per the What's New feed, api/whats-new-v2-amazon-aurora-s1000-p0: 'distributed SQL database with active-active high availability and multi-Region strong consistency'); if DSQL docs confirm synchronous cross-Region writes, option 2 becomes defensible for a 'managed relational database' and the question needs a stem change (for example name Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL). Rewrite the Twin to point to DynamoDB global tables with MRSC.
findings.resolution: fix-02: aws-map-q009 rewritten with q add --replace (rev 2, verification reset to candidate round 0, counted as questions_reset). Option b (synchronous replica in a second Region, impossible-feature resting on the stale fact) replaced by 'snapshots every few minutes kept in the same Region' (wrong-configuration, trap aws-map-trap-region-auto-replicates, grounded in no-automatic-cross-region-replication). Twin now: 'a Region failure must lose no committed write' -> the asynchronous replica no longer meets it (async fact). Explanation no longer cites the rejected fact. Key (a, c) unchanged; the item needs three fresh blind solves.

findings.section: card aws-map-c007 (type cannot, trap aws-map-trap-sync-replication-across-regions)
findings.quote: "front": "In AWS, can you replicate data synchronously from one Region to another Region?", "back": "No. Replication between Regions is asynchronous."
findings.evidence: full:amazondynamodb-developerguide: 'With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns'. The card's answer 'No' is now wrong for DynamoDB global tables in MRSC mode (GA June 30, 2025, DocumentHistory row). A flashcard that drills a false 'cannot' is worse than prose, because she will memorize it. Fix: change to a 'differ' card (DynamoDB global tables MREC vs MRSC: asynchronous vs synchronous, RPO zero) or narrow the front to a named service whose cross-Region copy is asynchronous (for example S3 Cross-Region Replication), each with a verified fact.
findings.resolution: fix-02: card aws-map-c007 replaced (cards add --replace) by a differ card: 'a synchronous standby in a second Availability Zone or an asynchronous replica in a second Region: which one can lose the latest writes in a failover?' -> 'The asynchronous replica in the second Region.', fact global-infrastructure-async-cross-region-replication-may-lose-data. No 'cannot' claim left.

findings.section: speak item aws-map-s02 (ten_second, key point kp4, must_not_say 2, follow-up 1)
findings.quote: "error": "We can copy the database synchronously to the other Region, so we lose nothing.", "correct": "AWS does not provide a synchronous cross-Region replication feature. A failover between Regions can lose data."
findings.evidence: The 'correct' line tells a founder something false: full:amazondynamodb-developerguide 'MRSC global tables support a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero.' and 'With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns'. As an AWS Startup SA she would say this in office hours to a customer who may already use DynamoDB MRSC. kp4 ('AWS does not provide a synchronous cross-Region replication feature, so a failover between Regions can lose data') and the ten-second answer ('expect asynchronous copies') carry the same error; follow-up 1 is fine only if scoped to asynchronous replication. Fix: 'Most cross-Region replication is asynchronous, so a failover can lose the last writes; if you need zero data loss across Regions, DynamoDB global tables offer multi-Region strong consistency, at higher write latency.' (MRSC latency: same guide, 'MRSC global tables will have higher write and strongly consistent read latencies compared to MREC global tables.')
findings.resolution: fix-02: speak aws-map-s02 replaced: ten_second ends 'an asynchronous copy there runs behind'; sixty_second line 'The thing to watch is that an asynchronous copy runs behind'; kp4, must_not_say 2 and follow-up 1 rewritten on the async fact (error line is now 'Our copy in the second Region is asynchronous, but a failover will lose nothing'); the rejected fact removed from every facts list. MRSC is not named (no verified fact).

findings.section: A second Region protects against Region failure but replicates asynchronously (plain table); also 1-fast.md Choose it or not, 'Several Availability Zones' column
findings.quote: | Survive an AZ failure | Multi-AZ | Synchronous |
findings.evidence: The linked fact global-infrastructure-az-latency-single-digit-ms says only that you CAN: 'You can replicate data synchronously between Availability Zones for most workloads without significantly impacting user experience.' It does not say that a Multi-AZ design copies synchronously. Many Multi-AZ copies are asynchronous (for example a read replica in another Availability Zone), and the exam tests exactly this difference (Multi-AZ standby versus read replica). The table equates 'Multi-AZ' with 'Synchronous' and the 1-fast cell 'Synchronous copies? ... Yes' does the same. Fix: 'Synchronous is possible' / 'Can be synchronous', and keep 'for most workloads' from the quote.
findings.resolution: fix-02: deep table cell is now 'Can be synchronous'; fast row label 'Synchronous copies possible?' with 'Yes: you can replicate data synchronously between Availability Zones'.

findings.section: Edge locations serve users nearby and Local Zones run compute near them (Exam trap aws-map-trap-edge-location-runs-workloads)
findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** An option launches EC2 instances "at an edge location". Your own compute goes into a Local Zone.
findings.evidence: No fact link, and the second sentence is too broad. Your own code does run at edge locations: www/cloudfront/faqs line 508 'CloudFront Functions is a serverless edge compute feature allowing you to run JavaScript code at CloudFront edge locations for lightweight HTTP(s) transformations and manipulations.' and www/lambda/faqs line 101 'Lambda@Edge allows you to run code across AWS locations globally without provisioning or managing servers, responding to end-users at the lowest network latency.' Own compute can also go to a Region, a Wavelength Zone or an Outpost (the chapter's own table). Fix: 'You cannot launch EC2 instances at an edge location; EC2 near one city goes into a Local Zone' (needs a fact for the first half, or keep it to the Local Zone half with its link), and mention edge functions in one line or xref the CloudFront chapter.
findings.resolution: fix-02: trap now 'Edge locations host services such as [Amazon CloudFront](pop fact); EC2 instances near one city go into a Local Zone.' The over-broad 'Your own compute goes into a Local Zone' is gone. Edge functions (CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge) are not mentioned: no verified fact in the canon; left to chapter 15.

findings.section: The best Region is near your users and meets your data rules (lead paragraph)
findings.quote: Regions differ in **latency** (LAY-ten-see), services, law and price. Check four things; AWS gives no fixed order.
findings.evidence: 'AWS gives no fixed order' is a claim about AWS guidance with no fact, and the chapter's own linked fact implies an order: well-architected-region-pricing-differs-choose-by-cost 'Identify Regional cost differences and only deploy in Regions with higher costs to meet latency, data residency and data sovereignty requirements.' (COST07-BP02): residency and latency come before price. The list then numbers data rules first, which contradicts 'no fixed order'. findings.section: The best Region is near your users and meets your data rules (Why line)
findings.quote: Why? Moving data between places costs money: [keep your data close to your customer and close to the resources](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-data-transfer-cost-keep-data-close).
findings.evidence: The first clause has no link and is too broad: verified fact global-infrastructure-inbound-transfer-no-charge-in-most-cases (docs/whitepapers/latest/how-aws-pricing-works/key-principles) 'In most cases, there is no charge for inbound data transfer or for data transfer between other AWS services within the same Region.' The cost driver is outbound transfer (fact global-infrastructure-three-cost-drivers: 'compute, storage, and outbound data transfer'). Cost questions on the exam turn on this difference. Fix: 'Data transfer out of AWS and between Regions costs money' with the outbound fact, or quote the COST07 sentence alone.
findings.resolution: fix-02: 'Moving data between places costs money' removed. The Why line is now 'The farther the Region, the longer each request travels.'

findings.quote: **FAQ 4.** Can AWS CloudShell keep your files between sessions? ... Yes, up to [1 GB](../facts/management-console.md#management-console-cloudshell-faq-home-directory-persists-1-gb-per-region) per Region.

findings.section: Question 10 (aws-map-q006), Why not option 2 (Local Zone)
findings.quote: - "Run the development and test EC2 instances in ...": The stem says latency is not a concern, and resources in Local Zones have [different prices than they do in parent AWS Regions](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-local-zones-pricing-no-enable-charge-different-prices).

A Local Zone is [an extension of an AWS Region in geographic proximity to your users], so it buys latency, not a lower price.'; fact added to the item's facts.
